_about: Recorded LIVE replies of POST /api/plan (GroqCloud, openai/gpt-oss-120b) on 2026-11-13, one request per question, during the product sprint. Kept exactly as the server returned them (proposal, model, warnings) so tests replay real model output; no key, prompt or personal data. Not predictions.

abroad.question: What if I moved to another country to pursue better career opportunities?
warnings: Left out 1 suggestion that was a research task, not a possible consequence. Things to find out stay in the questions.
Left out speculative claims that failed checks.

proposal.interpretation: You are considering relocating to a different country to improve your career prospects. I assumed you are evaluating whether to stay where you are or move abroad and how you would work there.

branches.name: Stay where you are
branches.description: Remain in your current country and seek career growth locally.

branches.name: Move and work locally
branches.description: Relocate to a new country and take a job that requires you to be physically present.

branches.name: Move and work remotely
branches.description: Relocate but keep a job that can be done from anywhere.

variables.label: Country you might move to
variables.why: The location influences work permits, cost of living and job market.

variables.label: Industry or profession
variables.why: Different fields have varying demand across countries.

variables.label: Can you work remotely in your role
variables.why: Remote eligibility changes the need for a local employer.

variables.label: Is a work visa needed
variables.why: Visa rules affect feasibility and timeline of moving.

questions: Which industry or profession are you targeting?
Do you currently have a job that can be performed remotely?
What are the main factors you consider important in a new country (e.g., language, culture, cost of living)?
Do you have any existing work permits or visas for other countries?
Are there specific countries you are already interested in?

possibilities.text: You keep your existing network and avoid the hassle of immigration.
Local job market may limit the speed or level of career advancement you hope for.
Being on‑site can open faster promotions and stronger professional connections.

missingEvidence: Information on work‑visa eligibility for your target country
Demand and salary data for your career field in the new location
Company policies on remote work for employees abroad
Cost‑of‑living comparison between your current and potential countries
limitations: The analysis does not account for personal relationships or family considerations.
It assumes you have the legal right to work in the target country if a visa is obtained.
Economic or political changes in either country could alter outcomes.

cafe.question: What if I opened a small café instead of continuing my current job?

proposal.interpretation: You are considering whether to start a small café instead of keeping your current employment. I assumed the comparison is about your personal finances and time commitment.

branches.name: Open Café
branches.description: Leave your current job and launch the café full‑time.

branches.name: Stay at Job
branches.description: Continue your current employment and do not open a café.

branches.name: Part‑time Café
branches.description: Keep your job and run the café only evenings or weekends.

variables.label: Current job salary
variables.why: Base income if you stay employed

variables.label: Café monthly operating costs
variables.why: Expenses needed to keep the café running

variables.label: Hours worked per week at current job
Hours spent on café per week
variables.why: Time you would need to manage the café

variables.label: Café location setting
variables.why: Location influences foot traffic and costs

variables.label: Food‑service license required
variables.why: Legal requirement that may affect start‑up effort

variables.label: Café operating mode
variables.why: Defines how intensively the café is run

questions: What is your current monthly net salary from your job?
What monthly revenue do you expect the café to generate?
What monthly operating costs (rent, supplies, staff, etc.) do you anticipate for the café?
How many hours per week do you currently work at your job?
How many hours per week could you realistically devote to the café in a part‑time arrangement?

formulas.label: Net café profit per month
formulas.explanation: Revenue minus operating costs gives the café’s monthly profit

formulas.label: Total weekly time commitment
formulas.explanation: Sum of job and café work hours shows overall workload

possibilities.text: You could earn more than your current salary if the café becomes popular.
Initial costs and the need for a food‑service license may strain cash flow.
Your income remains stable and you avoid the risks of starting a business.
You may miss out on a potentially rewarding entrepreneurial experience.
You keep a steady paycheck while testing the café concept with lower risk.
Balancing two roles could lead to long work weeks and fatigue.
The success of the café will depend heavily on location and local demand.

missingEvidence: Local market demand for a café in your chosen area
Exact cost of obtaining the required food‑service license
Projected foot traffic for each location type
Availability of reliable suppliers and their pricing
limitations: Financial outcomes depend on many variables not captured here, such as seasonal fluctuations.
Time estimates assume you can maintain consistent weekly hours.
Regulatory requirements may vary beyond the simple license flag.

selfStudy.question: What if I chose self-study instead of attending university?
warnings: Left out speculative claims that failed checks.

proposal.interpretation: You are wondering how your life might differ if you decide to learn on your own rather than enroll in a university program. I assumed you are comparing the overall impact on knowledge, costs, and future opportunities.

branches.name: Self‑study
branches.description: You rely on books, online courses, and personal projects to acquire the skills you need.

branches.name: University
branches.description: You enroll in a traditional campus program and follow the prescribed curriculum.

branches.name: Hybrid
branches.description: You combine a part‑time university enrollment with extensive self‑directed learning.

variables.label: Learning approach
variables.why: Determines the overall structure and resources you will use.

variables.label: Hours devoted to study each week
variables.why: Affects depth of knowledge and speed of progress.

variables.label: Desired career field
variables.why: Different fields value credentials and portfolios differently.

variables.label: Access to professional network through institution
variables.why: Networking can open job opportunities and mentorship.

questions: What field or industry do you aim to work in after learning?
How many hours per week can you realistically dedicate to studying?
Do you have a budget limit for education expenses?
How important is a formal credential for your intended career?
Do you value access to a campus‑based professional network?

possibilities.text: A recognized degree can open doors in fields that require accredited qualifications.
High tuition and fixed schedules may limit flexibility and increase financial pressure.
You gain a credential while still customizing much of your learning.
Balancing coursework with self‑directed projects can be demanding on time and energy.
Your ability to build a strong professional network will depend on how actively you seek mentorship and connections, regardless of the path.

missingEvidence: Information on employer expectations for credentials in your target industry
Cost breakdown of tuition, fees, and living expenses for university options
Availability of high‑quality self‑study resources for your chosen field
Opportunities for internships or practical experience in each path
limitations: Outcomes depend heavily on personal discipline and motivation
External factors such as job market conditions are not modeled
The analysis does not account for scholarships, loans, or financial aid
Networking benefits vary widely between institutions and individual effort
